questions.question: At how many maximum points can two distinct straight lines intersect on a plane?
questions.hint: Think about lines crossing each other.

options.explanation: Intersecting lines meet at least once.
Two distinct straight lines can intersect at a maximum of exactly one point.
Straight lines cannot curve to intersect twice.
Only identical (coincident) lines have infinite points of intersection.

questions.explanation: Two distinct straight lines on a plane can meet at a maximum of one single point. If they do not meet, they are parallel.

questions.question: What is the sum of the measures of two angles that form a linear pair?
questions.hint: A linear pair forms a straight line.

options.explanation: This is the sum of complementary angles.
Adjacent angles forming a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
This is a reflex angle measure.

questions.explanation: Adjacent angles formed by two lines intersecting each other on a straight line are called a linear pair. They always add up to $180^{\circ}$.

questions.question: If two lines intersect and one angle is $45^{\circ}$, what is the measure of its vertically opposite angle?
questions.hint: Vertically opposite angles have a specific relationship.

options.explanation: This would be the adjacent angle (linear pair), not the vertically opposite one.
This is the sum of a linear pair.

questions.explanation: When two lines intersect, vertically opposite angles are always equal to each other. Therefore, if one is $45^{\circ}$, the other is also $45^{\circ}$.

questions.question: What is the measure of each angle formed when two lines are perpendicular to each other?
questions.hint: Perpendicular lines form a square corner.

options.explanation: Perpendicular lines intersect at right angles.

questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines are a pair of lines which intersect each other at right angles, which measure exactly $90^{\circ}$.

questions.question: When a single transversal line intersects two distinct lines, how many angles are formed in total?
questions.hint: Count the angles at each intersection point.

options.explanation: This is the number of angles at a single intersection point.
Four angles at each of the two intersection points.

questions.explanation: A transversal intersecting two lines creates two intersection points. Each intersection point forms $4$ angles, resulting in a total of $8$ angles.

questions.question: Two angles form a linear pair. If their measures are $x$ and $x + 20^{\circ}$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.hint: Set their sum to $180^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Since the angles form a linear pair, $x + (x + 20^{\circ}) = 180^{\circ}$. Solving this gives $2x + 20^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \implies 2x = 160^{\circ} \implies x = 80^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Two lines intersect at a point. If one of the angles formed is $120^{\circ}$, what is the measure of an angle adjacent to it?
questions.hint: Adjacent angles on an intersecting line form a linear pair.

options.explanation: This is the vertically opposite angle, not the adjacent one.
This is the sum, not the individual angle.

questions.explanation: Adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines make a linear pair. Therefore, their sum is $180^{\circ}$. The adjacent angle is $180^{\circ} - 120^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines. If one angle is $135^{\circ}$, what is the measure of its alternate interior angle?
questions.hint: Alternate interior angles have a specific equality relationship.

options.explanation: This would be the consecutive interior angle.

questions.explanation: When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the alternate interior angles are always equal. Thus, the alternate interior angle is also $135^{\circ}$.

questions.question: The interior angles on the same side of a transversal intersecting two parallel lines measure $60^{\circ}$ and $z$. What is the value of $z$?
questions.hint: Interior angles on the same side are supplementary.
questions.explanation: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal intersecting parallel lines add up to $180^{\circ}$. Therefore, $z = 180^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 120^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Lines $l$ and $m$ are parallel, and transversal $t$ intersects them. If $\angle 1 = 50^{\circ}$, what is the measure of its corresponding angle?
questions.hint: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel.

options.explanation: This would be the adjacent linear pair.

questions.explanation: When a transversal intersects a pair of parallel lines, the corresponding angles are exactly equal to each other. So the angle is $50^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two lines. The alternate interior angles measure $70^{\circ}$ and $80^{\circ}$ respectively. Which of the following is true?
questions.hint: If the alternate interior angles are not equal, what does it mean about the lines?

options.explanation: Parallel lines must have equal alternate interior angles.

options.text: The lines are intersecting and not parallel.
options.explanation: Unequal alternate interior angles mean the lines are not parallel and will eventually intersect.

options.text: The transversal is perpendicular to the lines.
options.explanation: If it were perpendicular, the angles would be $90^{\circ}$.

questions.correctAnswer: The lines are intersecting and not parallel.
questions.explanation: For two lines to be parallel, the alternate interior angles formed by a transversal must be equal. Since $70^{\circ} \neq 80^{\circ}$, the lines are not parallel and will intersect.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines. A pair of corresponding angles measure $2x$ and $x + 30^{\circ}$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.hint: Corresponding angles are equal.

options.explanation: This is the angle itself, not $x$.

questions.explanation: Since the lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal. So, $2x = x + 30^{\circ}$. Subtracting $x$ from both sides gives $x = 30^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Two interior angles on the same side of a transversal intersecting two parallel lines measure $3x$ and $2x$. What are the measures of these two angles?
questions.hint: The sum of interior angles on the same side is $180^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Interior angles on the same side are supplementary. So, $3x + 2x = 180^{\circ} \implies 5x = 180^{\circ} \implies x = 36^{\circ}$. The angles are $3(36^{\circ}) = 108^{\circ}$ and $2(36^{\circ}) = 72^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Two lines intersect such that all four angles formed are equal. What is the measure of each angle?
questions.hint: The total sum around a point is $360^{\circ}$.

options.explanation: This is the total sum, not each angle.

questions.explanation: The sum of all four angles around a point of intersection is $360^{\circ}$. If they are all equal, each is $360^{\circ} / 4 = 90^{\circ}$. Such lines are perpendicular.

questions.question: Angles $a$ and $b$ form a linear pair. If $a = 2b$, what is the measure of angle $a$?
questions.hint: Substitute $a = 2b$ into the equation $a + b = 180^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: A linear pair sums to $180^{\circ}$, so $a + b = 180^{\circ}$. Substituting $a = 2b$ yields $2b + b = 180^{\circ} \implies 3b = 180^{\circ} \implies b = 60^{\circ}$. Since $a = 2b$, $a = 120^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines, making an angle of $90^{\circ}$ with one of the lines. What can be said about the other $7$ angles formed?
questions.hint: Use the properties of corresponding, alternate, and linear pair angles.

options.explanation: All corresponding and supplementary angles to $90^{\circ}$ are $90^{\circ}$.
We have enough information to find all angles.

questions.explanation: If one angle is $90^{\circ}$, its linear pair is $180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$. Its vertically opposite is $90^{\circ}$. Due to parallel lines, all corresponding and alternate angles are also equal to $90^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines. If one interior angle is $115^{\circ}$, what is the measure of the consecutive interior angle on the same side?
questions.hint: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary.

options.explanation: This would be the alternate interior angle.

questions.explanation: Interior angles on the same side of the transversal (consecutive interior angles) always add up to $180^{\circ}$. So, the other angle is $180^{\circ} - 115^{\circ} = 65^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Two vertically opposite angles measure $(3x - 10)^{\circ}$ and $(2x + 15)^{\circ}$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.hint: Equate the two expressions.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. So, $3x - 10 = 2x + 15$. Subtracting $2x$ from both sides gives $x - 10 = 15$. Adding $10$ yields $x = 25$.

questions.question: A line crosses two parallel lines. If one alternate exterior angle is $100^{\circ}$, what is the measure of the other alternate exterior angle?
questions.hint: Alternate exterior angles are equal when lines are parallel.

options.explanation: This would be the consecutive exterior angle.
This is their sum if they were supplementary.

questions.explanation: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, alternate exterior angles are equal in measure. So, the other alternate exterior angle is also $100^{\circ}$.

questions.question: If two adjacent angles form a linear pair and one angle is acute, what type of angle must the other be?
questions.hint: The sum of the angles must be $180^{\circ}$.

options.explanation: Two acute angles sum to less than $180^{\circ}$.
A right angle requires another right angle to make $180^{\circ}$.
An angle less than $90^{\circ}$ requires an angle greater than $90^{\circ}$ to sum to $180^{\circ}$.
A reflex angle is $> 180^{\circ}$, which is impossible here.

questions.explanation: A linear pair sums to $180^{\circ}$. If one angle is acute (less than $90^{\circ}$), the other must be greater than $90^{\circ}$ (obtuse) to reach a sum of exactly $180^{\circ}$.

questions.question: In a figure, lines $l$ and $m$ are parallel, and intersected by a transversal. If a pair of corresponding angles measure $(3x + 20)^{\circ}$ and $(4x - 10)^{\circ}$, what is the measure of these corresponding angles?
questions.hint: Equate the expressions to find $x$, then plug it back in.

options.explanation: This is the value of $x$, not the angle itself.

questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal. So, $3x + 20 = 4x - 10$. Subtracting $3x$ from both sides gives $x = 30$. Substituting $x$ back: $3(30) + 20 = 90 + 20 = 110^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Lines $p$ and $q$ are parallel. The interior angles on the same side of a transversal are $(x + 20)^{\circ}$ and $(2x - 50)^{\circ}$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.hint: The angles are supplementary.
questions.explanation: Interior angles on the same side are supplementary. So, $(x + 20) + (2x - 50) = 180$. Simplifying gives $3x - 30 = 180 \implies 3x = 210 \implies x = 70$.

questions.question: Two lines intersect to form four angles: $\angle a, \angle b, \angle c,$ and $\angle d$. If vertically opposite angles $\angle a$ and $\angle c$ sum to $200^{\circ}$, what is the measure of $\angle b$?
questions.hint: Find $\angle a$ first, then use the linear pair property to find $\angle b$.

options.explanation: $\angle a = 100^{\circ}$. Since $\angle a$ and $\angle b$ are a linear pair, $\angle b = 180^{\circ} - 100^{\circ} = 80^{\circ}$.
This is the measure of $\angle a$ or $\angle c$.
This is the sum of $\angle a$ and $\angle c$.

questions.explanation: Since $\angle a$ and $\angle c$ are vertically opposite, $\angle a = \angle c$. Their sum is $200^{\circ}$, meaning each is $100^{\circ}$. $\angle a$ and $\angle b$ form a linear pair, so $\angle b = 180^{\circ} - 100^{\circ} = 80^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Line $AB$ is parallel to line $CD$, and transversal $EF$ intersects them. If an interior angle $\angle AEF = 65^{\circ}$, what is the measure of the alternate interior angle $\angle DFE$?
questions.hint: Recall the property of alternate interior angles for parallel lines.

options.explanation: This is the consecutive interior angle.

questions.explanation: For parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal to each other. Thus, $\angle DFE = \angle AEF = 65^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines. The ratio of two interior angles on the same side of the transversal is $2:3$. What is the measure of the larger angle?
questions.hint: The angles add up to $180^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Let the angles be $2x$ and $3x$. Since they are supplementary, $2x + 3x = 180^{\circ} \implies 5x = 180^{\circ} \implies x = 36^{\circ}$. The larger angle is $3x = 3(36^{\circ}) = 108^{\circ}$.

questions.question: The ratio of the measures of two angles forming a linear pair is $4:5$. What is the positive difference between the two angles?
questions.hint: First, find the measures of the two angles.

options.explanation: The angles are $80^{\circ}$ and $100^{\circ}$. Difference is $20^{\circ}$.
This is the measure of the smaller angle.

questions.explanation: Let the angles be $4x$ and $5x$. Their sum is $180^{\circ}$. So $9x = 180^{\circ} \implies x = 20^{\circ}$. The angles are $80^{\circ}$ and $100^{\circ}$. The difference is $100^{\circ} - 80^{\circ} = 20^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines. A pair of alternate interior angles measure $(5y - 15)^{\circ}$ and $(3y + 25)^{\circ}$. What is the value of $y$?
questions.hint: Set the expressions equal to each other.
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal, so $5y - 15 = 3y + 25$. Subtracting $3y$ yields $2y - 15 = 25$. Adding $15$ gives $2y = 40 \implies y = 20$.

questions.question: In a quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB \parallel CD$ and $AD \parallel BC$. If $\angle ADC = 60^{\circ}$, what is the measure of $\angle BCD$?
questions.hint: Since $AD \parallel BC$, $CD$ acts as a transversal. What is the relation between $\angle ADC$ and $\angle BCD$?

options.explanation: This would be true for opposite angles $\angle ABC$.

questions.explanation: With $AD \parallel BC$, line segment $CD$ is a transversal. $\angle ADC$ and $\angle BCD$ are interior angles on the same side, so they sum to $180^{\circ}$. $\angle BCD = 180^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 120^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Lines $l, m,$ and $n$ are parallel to each other. A transversal intersects all three. If the alternate interior angle between $l$ and $m$ is $48^{\circ}$, what is the measure of the corresponding angle between $m$ and $n$?
questions.hint: Follow the equality of angles down the transversal.

options.explanation: Alternate interior angles equal the corresponding angles down the line.

questions.explanation: The alternate interior angle equals $48^{\circ}$, which means the angle on $m$ is $48^{\circ}$. Since $m \parallel n$, the corresponding angle on line $n$ is also equal to $48^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Lines $l$ and $m$ are parallel, intersected by a transversal $t$. One of the angles formed is $42^{\circ}$. What is the sum of its corresponding angle and its vertically opposite angle?
questions.hint: Find the measure of each of those two angles and add them together.
questions.explanation: The corresponding angle is $42^{\circ}$ (since lines are parallel). The vertically opposite angle to the original angle is also $42^{\circ}$. Their sum is $42^{\circ} + 42^{\circ} = 84^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Two straight lines intersect at a point. If the difference between two adjacent angles formed is $40^{\circ}$, what is the measure of the smaller angle?
questions.hint: Set up a system of equations: $a + b = 180^{\circ}$ and $a - b = 40^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Let the angles be $a$ and $b$. We know $a + b = 180^{\circ}$ (linear pair). We are given $a - b = 40^{\circ}$. Adding both equations: $2a = 220^{\circ} \implies a = 110^{\circ}$. Then $b = 180^{\circ} - 110^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal intersects lines $l$ and $m$. The interior angles on the same side of the transversal measure $120^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$. Which of the following is correct?
questions.hint: Add the interior angles on the same side.

options.explanation: If the sum is exactly $180^{\circ}$, they do not intersect.

options.text: The lines $l$ and $m$ are parallel because the sum of corresponding angles is $180^{\circ}$.
options.explanation: The given angles are not corresponding angles.

options.text: The lines $l$ and $m$ are parallel because the interior angles on the same side add up to $180^{\circ}$.
options.explanation: $120^{\circ} + 60^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$, which proves the lines are parallel.

questions.correctAnswer: The lines $l$ and $m$ are parallel because the interior angles on the same side add up to $180^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Since $120^{\circ} + 60^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$, the consecutive interior angles are supplementary. This is the necessary condition for lines $l$ and $m$ to be parallel.

questions.question: In a figure, lines $l \parallel m$. An angle $a = 120^{\circ}$. What is the measure of the vertically opposite angle of its alternate interior angle?
questions.hint: Find the alternate interior angle first.

options.explanation: This would be the linear pair angle.
Alternate interior is $120^{\circ}$. Its vertically opposite is $120^{\circ}$.

questions.explanation: The alternate interior angle to $a = 120^{\circ}$ is also $120^{\circ}$. The vertically opposite angle of this alternate interior angle is equal to itself, so it is also $120^{\circ}$.

questions.question: Two angles form a linear pair: $\angle PQR = (3x + 15)^{\circ}$ and $\angle RQS = (x + 5)^{\circ}$. What is the measure of $\angle PQR$?
questions.hint: Set their sum to $180^{\circ}$ to find $x$, then calculate $\angle PQR$.
questions.explanation: $(3x + 15) + (x + 5) = 180^{\circ} \implies 4x + 20 = 180 \implies 4x = 160 \implies x = 40$. Substitute $x = 40$ back into $\angle PQR = 3(40) + 15 = 135^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A transversal $t$ crosses parallel lines $l$ and $m$. If the sum of a pair of alternate interior angles is $150^{\circ}$, what is the pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal?
questions.hint: Find the measure of one alternate interior angle, then find its consecutive interior angle.

options.explanation: The interior angle is $75^{\circ}$ and the one on the same side is $180^{\circ} - 75^{\circ} = 105^{\circ}$.
These are the alternate interior angles, not the same-side interior angles.

questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal. Their sum is $150^{\circ}$, so each alternate interior angle is $75^{\circ}$. The interior angles on the same side of the transversal sum to $180^{\circ}$. Therefore, the pair consists of $75^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ} - 75^{\circ} = 105^{\circ}$.
